D5·gweg — 2026-09-15
rule: `sofar tune` never writes anything and never runs without `--dry-run`; a persisting or applying surface must be a separately named command, and a detector must never print a number for a signal the availability map calls unavailable on the clone.
chose: `sofar tune` has exactly one mode and it must be spelled: `--dry-run` is REQUIRED, the command refuses without it and writes nothing (no event, no row, no file under .sofar or the store). Detectors are pure functions over (raw events, diagnostics rows, availability map) with no filesystem or clock, so the report is byte-deterministic for the same inputs and replayable against a log prefix; the JSON is version-stamped and carries the corpus (events per initiative, rows, cutoff id). A detector runs only for a signal the map does not call unavailable on this clone; everything else is UNKNOWN with the map's reason and the missing requirement. Evidence is event ids or `row:`+sha256[0:16] of the stored row line. No detector names a cause and none proposes anything.
over: A default mode that detects AND persists suggestions (the audit's S5 warning about repeated tune calls re-emitting the same proposal); detectors reading the filesystem directly; a report stamped with the run time; printing 0 for a signal the clone has no shim for.
because: Audit S1/S3/S5: a count for an unobserved signal is confident nonsense, a re-derivation is not evidence, and a persistence mode hidden behind a default lets a shell history lie about what an invocation did. Purity buys replay (2.2 will replay detectors against held-out logs) and the determinism test buys the byte-identical assertion; the raw log rather than the fold is required because the fold deduplicates exactly the duplicate session starts one detector counts.
